title: Coastal beach-house porch, one recessed white heater in the recess kit, centred over the seating
kind: CAD composite on a generated Coastal plate
source: Plate ts2-r8e-03 (owner-approved Coastal plate; owner 22 Nov: 'One heater is fine here', recessed, recess kit always, centred over the seating). One Series II 6 kW, white, in the recess kit from the '6kW heater and recess kit' CAD (the kit's only trim part is BMC-00659, marked obsolete in the CAD), flush with the beadboard. The heater is set 30 mm up inside the kit so its curved near lip stays inside the trim, and the BROMIC end-cap logo shows upright above the vent. Long axis runs with the boards, centred on the seating group (sofa, two armchairs, coffee table) as solved from the camera (one-point view, f about 5000 px; ceiling about 2.8 m), about 1.4 m clear of the crown molding. Elements deep orange (about 192/105/51), face matched to the shaded ceiling, clean grille edge, no open hollow.

title: Coastal deck under a timber soffit, two recessed graphite heaters in the recess kit, centred over the seating
kind: CAD composite on a generated Coastal plate
source: Plate ts2-r8e-04 (owner-approved Coastal plate; owner 22 Nov: 'recessed gray or inward facing 2 heaters mounted from the long edge'; recess kit always; pair centred over the seating). The long-edge option (short posts at the fascia side, tilted inward) was rendered in round 1 and reads end-on from this camera, so the recessed option is used. Two Series II 6 kW, graphite, each in the recess kit as the CAD gives it (trim BMC-00659, marked obsolete in the CAD). They run in line along the boards with about 0.5 m between kits, centred on the sofa and lounge chair group, mid-soffit (about 1.3 m from the house wall). Contact occlusion is at the trim. Camera from the board/fascia vanishing point and the siding verticals (f about 4030 px); ceiling about 2.75 m. Graphite measured R>G>B (R/B 1.17), elements deep orange. The heaters are about 6% of the frame width; the logo is too small to read from this camera. NOTE: fails on size (M4) and logo legibility; from this camera no layout over the seats can fix it. Kept for the owner to judge.
